synthesis:draft.headline: POE50 vs actual for SA1 (2026-07-30 11:00 UTC—23:00 UTC): MAE 32.88 MW (ev1565); largest half-hour error 66.0 MW (ev1503).
summary: The 24 half-hour POE50 vs actual comparison for SA1 (2026-07-30T11:00:00Z—2026-07-30T23:00:00Z) gives MAE = 32.88 MW and mean error = 4.88 MW (ev1565, ev1566).
The single largest absolute half-hour error was 66.0 MW (4.2%) at 2026-07-30T15:30:00Z (local 2026-07-31 01:00 ACST) (ev1503, ev1504).
At the 5-minute dispatch-price peak (interval end 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z / 02:05 ACST) RRP = 4981.0 $/MWh and DISPATCH_TOTALDEMAND = 1472.82 MW (ev0964, ev0965).
For the 16:30 half-hour the POE50 was 1559.0 MW, actual operational demand 1509.0 MW, error 50.0 MW (ev1509, ev1510, ev1511).
Actual half-hour operational demand sample: interval-ending 2026-07-30T22:30:00Z operational_demand_mw = 2100.0 (ev0530).
Market notices retrieved include a Forecast LOR1 notice and LOR2 cancellation for SA1 on 29/07/2026; representative passages are cited below (market_notice_144652, market_notice_144628) [c1] [c2].

possible_explanations.statement: The forecast errors (MAE 32.88 MW, ev1565) may reflect routine short-term forecast uncertainty in a system with variable renewables and changing dispatch conditions.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare generator output/availability and actual wind/solar production for the same intervals; if forecast errors correlate with renewable output deviations or generator availability changes, that would support this explanation.

possible_explanations.statement: The very high 5-minute RRP at 16:35 UTC (4981.0 $/MWh, ev0964) might indicate locally tight supply conditions or scarce dispatchable capacity during that dispatch period.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Examine unit outage/availability records and interconnector capability/dispatchable capacity for the dispatch intervals around 16:35 UTC; finding reduced available capacity or outages concurrent with the price spike would support this hypothesis.

possible_explanations.statement: The largest half-hour forecast error (66.0 MW at 15:30 UTC, ev1503) could be associated with abrupt changes in demand drivers (for example temperature swings) and might be tested against weather observations (Adelaide T2M values ev1440, ev1433).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare high-resolution temperature, solar irradiance and observed load shape for Adelaide/SA1 around the 15:30 UTC interval; a mismatch between expected and observed weather-linked load would support this explanation.
